pack.description: Functional language: connectors, hedging, agreement and disagreement, signposts for spoken answers, and email formulas for requests, complaints, apologies, follow-ups and recommendations.
pack.selection_note: Internal high-yield selection of connectors and formulas for the Email, Academic Discussion and Interview tasks; this is not an official list and CEFR levels are author estimates.
pack.copyright_policy: Original content written for this app. No dictionary definition, ETS item or external word list was copied.

entries.definition: for the reason that has just been given
entries.example_academic: The sample was small; the results should therefore be interpreted with caution.
entries.example_spoken: I missed the bus and therefore got to class late.

entries.definition: used to introduce what happened because of the thing just mentioned
entries.example_academic: Rainfall declined for a decade; as a result, harvests fell by a third.
entries.example_spoken: I stayed up all night and, as a result, I slept through my alarm.

entries.definition: because of something
entries.translation_fr: en raison de, à cause de
entries.example_academic: The delay was due to a shortage of qualified engineers.
entries.example_spoken: The game was cancelled due to rain.

entries.definition: used to give the reason for something
entries.example_academic: Many species have disappeared because of habitat loss.
entries.example_spoken: I was late because of the traffic.

entries.definition: to cause something to happen or exist
entries.example_academic: Overuse of antibiotics can lead to resistant strains of bacteria.
entries.example_spoken: Skipping breakfast always leads to a bad morning for me.

entries.definition: as a result of what has just been said
entries.example_academic: Funding was withdrawn, and consequently the project was abandoned.
entries.example_spoken: My laptop broke and, consequently, I lost half my notes.

entries.definition: as a result of this; or in this way
entries.example_academic: The two groups never met and thus developed separate dialects.
entries.example_spoken: He practiced every day and thus improved quickly.

entries.definition: for this reason; used to introduce a result or an explanation of a name
entries.example_academic: The metal expands when heated; hence the gaps left between the rails.
entries.example_spoken: The café is in an old bank, hence the name "The Vault."

entries.definition: to be caused by something; to have something as its origin
entries.example_academic: Many of the errors stem from a misunderstanding of the original text.
entries.example_spoken: Most of our arguments stem from who does the dishes.

entries.definition: to cause something to happen or exist
entries.example_academic: The discovery gave rise to an entirely new field of research.
entries.example_spoken: That rule change gave rise to a lot of complaints.

entries.definition: happening after and often because of an important event
entries.translation_fr: à la suite de, dans le sillage de
entries.example_academic: In the wake of the crisis, regulators tightened the rules on lending.
entries.example_spoken: In the wake of the scandal, the coach resigned.

entries.definition: used to introduce a fact that makes the main statement surprising
entries.example_academic: Although the method is expensive, it yields far more reliable data.
entries.example_spoken: Although I studied a lot, I found the exam hard.

entries.definition: used to introduce a statement that contrasts with what has just been said
entries.example_academic: The theory is elegant; however, it has never been tested.
entries.example_spoken: I like the course. However, the workload is heavy.

entries.definition: used to stress that something is true in spite of the fact that follows
entries.example_academic: Even though emissions fell, concentrations in the atmosphere continued to rise.
entries.example_spoken: I went to class even though I had a cold.

entries.definition: without being prevented or affected by something
entries.example_academic: Despite its small size, the country exports a wide range of goods.
entries.example_spoken: We had a good time despite the weather.

entries.definition: used to introduce a different or opposite point of view
entries.example_academic: Nuclear power produces little carbon; on the other hand, its waste remains dangerous for centuries.
entries.example_spoken: The apartment is cheap. On the other hand, it's far from campus.

entries.definition: in spite of what has just been said
entries.example_academic: The evidence is incomplete; nevertheless, a pattern is beginning to emerge.
entries.example_spoken: It was raining; nevertheless, we went for a run.

entries.definition: used to compare two facts and show that they are different
entries.example_academic: Mammals regulate their body temperature, whereas reptiles depend on external heat.
entries.example_spoken: I like mornings, whereas my roommate works best at night.

entries.definition: used to contrast two facts, or to admit one point before making another
entries.example_academic: While the reform reduced costs, it also lowered the quality of service.
entries.example_spoken: While I see the advantages, I still prefer the old system.

entries.definition: in spite of what has just been mentioned
entries.example_academic: The task was difficult; the team nonetheless completed it on time.
entries.example_spoken: It's a small improvement, but nonetheless it's progress.

entries.definition: used to add information that slightly reduces the force of what has just been said
entries.example_academic: The economy continued to grow, albeit at a slower pace.
entries.example_spoken: I finished the essay, albeit two hours late.

entries.definition: used before adding a point that limits or contrasts with what you have just stated
entries.example_academic: The survey has clear weaknesses. That said, it remains the best source available.
entries.example_spoken: The class is tough. That said, I'm learning a lot.

entries.definition: without being affected by something; in spite of
entries.example_academic: Notwithstanding these limitations, the study makes an important contribution.
entries.example_spoken: Notwithstanding the rain, the ceremony went ahead outside.

entries.definition: used to accept that something may be true before saying it does not change your view
entries.example_academic: Costs have certainly risen. Be that as it may, the investment remains justified.
entries.example_spoken: You say he's busy. Be that as it may, he should have answered.

entries.definition: partly, but not completely
entries.example_academic: The decline can be explained, to some extent, by changes in diet.
entries.example_spoken: To some extent, I think the professor is right.

entries.definition: usually, though not always
entries.example_academic: In most cases, the infection clears without treatment.
entries.example_spoken: In most cases, I just email the professor directly.

entries.definition: used to say that something will probably happen or is probably true
entries.example_academic: It is likely that the tools were made elsewhere and brought to the site.
entries.example_spoken: It is likely that the exam will be moved to Friday.

entries.definition: used to say that something is true in most situations
entries.example_academic: Generally speaking, larger firms invest more in training.
entries.example_spoken: Generally speaking, I prefer working in a group.

entries.definition: used when giving an opinion that you believe could be supported with good reasons
entries.translation_fr: sans doute, on peut soutenir que
entries.example_academic: This is arguably the most influential experiment in the history of the field.
entries.example_spoken: It's arguably the best café near campus.

entries.definition: used to say what you think is probably true although you are not certain
entries.example_academic: The settlement was abandoned, presumably because the wells ran dry.
entries.example_spoken: Presumably she got my message, since she showed up.

entries.definition: used to introduce a view that is reasonable but that you do not state as certain
entries.example_academic: It could be argued that the reform simply moved the problem elsewhere.
entries.example_spoken: It could be argued that group work wastes more time than it saves.

entries.definition: used to say that something is very probably true or will very probably happen
entries.example_academic: In all likelihood, the manuscript was copied in a northern monastery.
entries.example_spoken: In all likelihood, they'll cancel the Friday session.

entries.definition: in general; when everything is considered
entries.example_academic: By and large, the predictions of the model have been confirmed.
entries.example_spoken: By and large, I'm happy with my schedule.

entries.definition: to the degree that
entries.example_academic: The policy succeeded insofar as it reduced unemployment among the young.
entries.example_spoken: I'll help insofar as my schedule allows.

entries.definition: used to add a warning or limit to what you have just said
entries.example_academic: The results are encouraging, with the caveat that the sample was small.
entries.example_spoken: I recommend the course, with the caveat that it takes a lot of time.

entries.definition: used to say that you understand someone's opinion, often before disagreeing in part
entries.translation_fr: je vois ce que vous voulez dire
entries.example_academic: I see your point about cost; my concern, however, is with safety.
entries.example_spoken: I see your point, but I still think we should start earlier.

entries.definition: used to accept that what someone has said is reasonable
entries.example_academic: That's a fair point, and the revised draft now addresses it directly.
entries.example_spoken: That's a fair point; I hadn't thought about the cost.

entries.definition: a polite way of saying that you doubt or disagree with something
entries.translation_fr: je n'en suis pas si sûr
entries.example_academic: I'm not sure about that; the figures in the second table suggest the opposite.
entries.example_spoken: I'm not sure about that. Didn't the professor say Thursday?

entries.definition: used to say that you understand what someone is trying to say
entries.translation_fr: je vois ce que tu veux dire
entries.example_academic: I see what you mean, although the author's definition is narrower than yours.
entries.example_spoken: Oh, I see what you mean: the two graphs don't match.

entries.definition: used to say that you agree completely
entries.example_academic: I couldn't agree more with the reviewer's comment on the sample size.
entries.example_spoken: I couldn't agree more; that lecture was way too long.

entries.definition: a polite phrase used before disagreeing with or criticizing someone
entries.translation_fr: sauf votre respect, avec tout le respect que je vous dois
entries.example_academic: With all due respect, the committee has overlooked a crucial piece of evidence.
entries.example_spoken: With all due respect, I don't think that plan will work.

entries.definition: a polite and rather formal way of saying that you disagree
entries.translation_fr: permettez-moi de ne pas être d'accord
entries.example_academic: The author claims the question is settled; I beg to differ.
entries.example_spoken: You think the test was easy? I beg to differ.

entries.definition: used to say that you mostly agree, without being completely certain
entries.example_academic: I'm inclined to agree with the second reviewer that the title is misleading.
entries.example_spoken: I'm inclined to agree with you, but let's hear what Sam thinks.

entries.definition: to agree with someone or have the same opinion
entries.translation_fr: être du même avis, souscrire à
entries.example_academic: Most specialists concur that the document is a later forgery.
entries.example_spoken: I concur with everything she just said.

entries.definition: to disagree with something that someone has said or done
entries.example_academic: Several historians take issue with this reading of the sources.
entries.example_spoken: I take issue with the idea that we didn't work hard enough.

entries.definition: used to introduce the first of several points
entries.example_academic: First of all, the study defines what it means by poverty.
entries.example_spoken: First of all, I'd like to thank everyone for coming.

entries.definition: used to introduce an example
entries.example_academic: Some metals, for instance copper, conduct heat extremely well.
entries.example_spoken: You could, for instance, record yourself and listen back.

entries.definition: used to show that what follows is what you think
entries.example_academic: In my opinion, the second explanation accounts for more of the evidence.
entries.example_spoken: In my opinion, online classes work better for big lectures.

entries.definition: used to say something again in a simpler or clearer way
entries.example_academic: The gene is recessive; in other words, both parents must carry it.
entries.example_spoken: He never replied. In other words, we're on our own.

entries.definition: used to explain more clearly something you have just said
entries.translation_fr: ce que je veux dire, c'est que
entries.example_academic: What I mean is that the two processes cannot be studied separately.
entries.example_spoken: What I mean is, we should split the work more fairly.

entries.definition: in addition to what has just been mentioned
entries.translation_fr: en plus de cela, par-dessus le marché
entries.example_academic: Yields were poor, and on top of that, transport costs doubled.
entries.example_spoken: I have two essays due and, on top of that, a shift on Saturday.

entries.definition: used to introduce a short statement of the main points
entries.example_academic: To sum up, the evidence favors the second hypothesis.
entries.example_spoken: To sum up, I think living on campus is worth the cost.

entries.definition: used to add another fact or point
entries.example_academic: In addition, the survey recorded the age and occupation of each respondent.
entries.example_spoken: In addition, we'd need someone to book the room.

entries.definition: used to add information that supports what has just been said
entries.example_academic: The method is cheap; moreover, it requires no special equipment.
entries.example_spoken: The room is too small and, moreover, it has no projector.

entries.definition: used to say that you think something is true but you are not completely sure
entries.example_academic: As far as I know, no comparable study has been carried out.
entries.example_spoken: As far as I know, the library closes at ten.

entries.definition: used to give your personal opinion about something
entries.example_academic: As far as I'm concerned, the second proposal is the stronger of the two.
entries.example_spoken: As far as I'm concerned, we can meet any day but Friday.

entries.definition: in addition to what has just been stated
entries.example_academic: The data are incomplete; furthermore, they were collected by different methods.
entries.example_spoken: It's expensive and, furthermore, it's a long way from campus.

entries.definition: used before explaining something again in different words
entries.translation_fr: autrement dit, pour le dire autrement
entries.example_academic: To put it another way, growth without investment cannot last.
entries.example_spoken: To put it another way, we have three days and ten chapters.

entries.definition: concerning a particular subject
entries.translation_fr: en ce qui concerne, quant à
entries.example_academic: With regard to funding, the report recommends no immediate change.
entries.example_spoken: With regard to your question, I'll check and get back to you.

entries.definition: used to give a judgment after thinking about every part of a situation
entries.example_academic: All things considered, the benefits of the program outweigh its costs.
entries.example_spoken: All things considered, the presentation went pretty well.

entries.definition: used to say that you will give only the main point and no more detail
entries.example_academic: Suffice it to say that the two accounts cannot both be accurate.
entries.example_spoken: Suffice it to say, the group meeting did not go well.

entries.definition: a standard way of beginning a formal email by stating why you are sending it
entries.example_academic: I am writing to request an extension for the research proposal.
entries.example_spoken: I started with "I am writing to ask about my application"; is that too formal?

entries.definition: a polite way of asking someone to do something
entries.example_academic: Could you please confirm whether the seminar room is available on Tuesday?
entries.example_spoken: Could you please send me the slides after class?

entries.definition: a polite way of asking for something by saying you would be thankful for it
entries.translation_fr: je vous serais reconnaissant de bien vouloir
entries.example_academic: I would appreciate it if you could send me the reading list in advance.
entries.example_spoken: I would really appreciate it if you could look at my draft.

entries.definition: a soft, polite way of introducing a request or question
entries.example_academic: I was wondering if it would be possible to reschedule our meeting.
entries.example_spoken: I was wondering if you could lend me your notes.

entries.definition: a polite way of asking whether something can be done
entries.example_academic: Would it be possible to submit the form by post rather than online?
entries.example_spoken: Would it be possible to move my shift to Sunday?

entries.definition: a formal and polite way of asking someone to do something
entries.example_academic: I would be grateful if you could confirm receipt of this application.
entries.example_spoken: I ended the email with "I would be grateful if you could reply by Friday."

entries.definition: as soon as you are able to, without being rushed
entries.translation_fr: dès que cela vous sera possible
entries.example_academic: Please return the signed form at your earliest convenience.
entries.example_spoken: She told me to call back at your earliest convenience, which sounded very official.

entries.headword: should you need any further information
entries.definition: a formal way of offering to give more details if the reader wants them
entries.translation_fr: si vous avez besoin de renseignements complémentaires
entries.example_academic: Should you need any further information, please do not hesitate to contact me.
entries.example_spoken: I closed with "Should you need any further information, I'm happy to help."

entries.headword: I would be much obliged if
entries.definition: a very formal way of asking for something, expressing thanks in advance
entries.translation_fr: je vous serais très obligé de
entries.example_academic: I would be much obliged if you could forward this request to the committee.
entries.example_spoken: My grandfather still writes "I would be much obliged if you could reply."
synonyms: I would be most grateful if

entries.definition: used to say that something is sad, disappointing or has a bad effect
entries.example_academic: Unfortunately, the heating in the apartment has not worked since Monday.
entries.example_spoken: Unfortunately, I can't make it to the meeting.

entries.definition: used to tell someone that a result or service was worse than you expected
entries.example_academic: I am disappointed that my earlier message has not received a reply.
entries.example_spoken: I am disappointed that nobody told us about the change.

entries.definition: used in a formal message to say that you are worried about a situation
entries.translation_fr: faire part de mon inquiétude au sujet de
entries.example_academic: I am writing to express my concern about the noise from the construction site.
entries.example_spoken: I wanted to express my concern about how the groups were chosen.

entries.definition: to fail to reach a standard or level that was expected
entries.translation_fr: ne pas être à la hauteur de
entries.example_academic: The quality of the accommodation fell short of what was advertised.
entries.example_spoken: The workshop fell short of my expectations.

entries.definition: used to say that something made you feel shocked and disappointed
entries.example_academic: To my dismay, the order arrived three weeks late and incomplete.
entries.example_spoken: To my dismay, the printer broke an hour before the deadline.

entries.definition: to correct something that is wrong
entries.example_academic: I trust that you will take steps to rectify the situation promptly.
entries.example_spoken: They promised to rectify the mistake on my bill.

entries.headword: leave a great deal to be desired
entries.definition: to be much worse than it should be
entries.example_academic: The cleanliness of the shared kitchen leaves a great deal to be desired.
entries.example_spoken: Honestly, the food in that cafeteria leaves a great deal to be desired.
entries.ipa: /liːv ə ˈɡreɪt ˌdiːl tə bi dɪˈzaɪərd/

entries.definition: used to say that you are sorry about something you did or caused
entries.translation_fr: je vous prie d'excuser, je m'excuse de
entries.example_academic: I apologize for the delay in replying to your message.
entries.example_spoken: I apologize for being late; my bus broke down.

entries.definition: used to say you regret having caused someone trouble or extra work
entries.example_academic: I am sorry for the inconvenience this change may cause.
entries.example_spoken: Sorry for the inconvenience, but could we meet an hour later?

entries.definition: a formal way of saying that you are sorry
entries.example_academic: Please accept my apologies for missing yesterday's appointment.
entries.example_spoken: I wrote "Please accept my apologies" because I'd forgotten the meeting completely.

entries.headword: I regret to inform you that
entries.definition: a formal way of introducing bad news
entries.translation_fr: j'ai le regret de vous informer que
entries.example_academic: I regret to inform you that I will be unable to attend the conference.
entries.example_spoken: The letter began "I regret to inform you that your application was unsuccessful."

entries.definition: events that nobody expected and that cause a change of plan
entries.example_academic: Due to unforeseen circumstances, the lecture has been postponed until next week.
entries.example_spoken: I had to cancel because of unforeseen circumstances at home.

entries.definition: used to say that you accept that a problem was your fault
entries.example_academic: I take full responsibility for the error in the submitted figures.
entries.example_spoken: I take full responsibility for the mix-up with the room booking.

entries.definition: by accident, without intending to
entries.example_academic: I inadvertently attached an earlier version of the report to my message.
entries.example_spoken: I inadvertently deleted the whole folder.

entries.definition: used to say that you are writing again about something discussed or requested earlier
entries.translation_fr: je reviens vers vous au sujet de
entries.example_academic: I am following up on the request I submitted on the third of March.
entries.example_spoken: I am following up on my email from last week; did you get it?

entries.headword: I look forward to hearing from you
entries.definition: a polite closing line that shows you expect a reply
entries.example_academic: Thank you for your help; I look forward to hearing from you.
entries.example_spoken: I always end with "I look forward to hearing from you."
entries.ipa: /aɪ lʊk ˈfɔːrwərd tə ˌhɪrɪŋ frʌm juː/

entries.definition: a polite way of asking someone to tell you something
entries.example_academic: Please let me know whether Thursday afternoon would be convenient.
entries.example_spoken: Please let me know if you need a ride.

entries.definition: used to refer back to something you have already said or written
entries.example_academic: As I mentioned in my previous message, the form requires your signature.
entries.example_spoken: As I mentioned, I'll be away next week.

entries.definition: used in formal letters and emails to refer to an earlier message or conversation
entries.example_academic: Further to our conversation on Monday, I attach the documents you requested.
entries.example_spoken: He wrote "Further to our call" at the top, which is how they start emails there.

entries.definition: used to say what a formal message is about
entries.translation_fr: au sujet de, en référence à
entries.example_academic: I am writing in reference to the vacancy advertised on your website.
entries.example_spoken: I'm calling in reference to the apartment on Maple Street.

entries.definition: to ask politely how far something, such as an application, has progressed
entries.translation_fr: se renseigner sur l'état d'avancement de
entries.example_academic: I would like to inquire about the status of my scholarship application.
entries.example_spoken: I called to inquire about the status of my refund.

entries.definition: following or according to a rule, agreement or earlier message
entries.example_academic: Pursuant to our agreement of the tenth of May, I enclose the signed contract.
entries.example_spoken: The notice said "pursuant to the housing rules," which just means the rules require it.

entries.definition: used to give advice about what someone should do or choose
entries.example_academic: I would recommend extending the opening hours of the library during examinations.
entries.example_spoken: I would recommend the Tuesday section; the instructor is great.

entries.definition: used to put forward an idea or plan for someone to consider
entries.example_academic: I suggest that the committee postpone the decision until all members are present.
entries.example_spoken: I suggest that we meet at the library instead.

entries.headword: it might be a good idea to
entries.definition: a gentle way of advising someone to do something
entries.translation_fr: ce serait peut-être une bonne idée de
entries.example_academic: It might be a good idea to send a reminder a week before the event.
entries.example_spoken: It might be a good idea to book the room now.
entries.ipa: /ɪt maɪt bi ə ˌɡʊd aɪˈdiːə tuː/

entries.definition: used to offer one possible solution among several
entries.example_academic: One option would be to divide the class into two smaller groups.
entries.example_spoken: One option would be to record the meeting for people who can't come.

entries.definition: used to give firm advice
entries.example_academic: I strongly advise new students to attend the orientation session.
entries.example_spoken: I strongly advise you to start the reading early.

entries.definition: a formal way of saying that doing something is sensible
entries.example_academic: It would be advisable to inform all tenants before the work begins.
entries.example_spoken: It would be advisable to check with your advisor first.

entries.definition: used to advise someone very strongly to do something
entries.example_academic: I would urge you to reconsider the decision to close the reading room.
entries.example_spoken: I would urge you to apply even if you think your grades are too low.

entries.definition: a formal way of saying that an action is careful and sensible given the risks
entries.example_academic: It would be prudent to obtain a second estimate before approving the repairs.
entries.example_spoken: It would be prudent to save a copy before you change anything.
